name: AI Response Rendering Pattern
description: How to render an AI assistant's reply as it streams in: a typed block list for text, code, tool calls, citations, artifacts, and optional reasoning; one DOM update per frame; Stop that keeps what arrived; errors shown in place; model output treated as untrusted; and one polite status region instead of announcing every token. Companion to the AI Agent Chat Layout.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Render an AI assistant's reply as an ordered list of typed blocks that grows as the stream arrives. Build on the project's message renderer, Markdown renderer, and sanitizer when it has them, and on the typed message parts its AI SDK provides, if any. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and add no dependency without asking. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility, security, or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA. In a chat, the host (for example the AI Agent Chat Layout) owns the Stop button, Edit, scrolling, and the conversation's status region; this pattern owns the inside of each assistant message.
keyFeatures: A typed block list (text, code, tool-call, citation, artifact-ref, error, and optional reasoning), never one growing string
Stream deltas grow the trailing block, the DOM updates at most once per animation frame, and finished blocks never re-render

Model output treated as untrusted: sanitized Markdown, links only for http, https, and mailto, images only from allowed hosts, and HTML artifacts in a sandbox, with policies that keep them from loading from or navigating to other hosts
Tool calls as cards with lifecycle states and stable ids
Citations as numbered links with a preview, and a source list for three or more sources
Stop keeps what arrived, and errors show in place with the partial content and a retry
Copy, Regenerate, and feedback controls with names and 24 px targets
One polite status region announces when a reply starts, runs a tool, ends, or fails, never the streamed text
Reasoning only when the provider exposes it and the product chooses to show it, as a short status by default
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection), plus the project's message and Markdown renderers, its sanitizer, and its AI SDK's message format. Build on what's there, and keep its APIs.
2. Map the stream to the block model and the reply lifecycle (implementationDetails.blockModel and messageLifecycle). If the SDK already sends typed parts, map those instead of parsing text.
3. Grow the trailing block as deltas arrive, at most once per animation frame (implementationDetails.streaming, frameworkPatterns.frameBatching).
5. Render the tool-call cards, citations, artifact cards, and error blocks the task needs, and reasoning only when the product needs it (implementationDetails).
6. Add the per-message controls, and Stop when the host has none (implementationDetails.controls).
7. Announce lifecycle changes through the conversation's status region (patternSpec.accessibility.screenReader).
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, and reduced motion, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

patternSpec.problem: An assistant's reply arrives as a stream of events: text deltas, tool calls and their results, citations, artifacts, stop reasons, and with some providers a reasoning channel. Rendered naively, the page shifts on every token, unfinished Markdown breaks, tool calls show as raw JSON, citations are bare numbers, Stop or an error loses what arrived, screen readers hear every token, and untrusted output can run script or send data to another site.
patternSpec.solution: Treat the reply as a state machine over an ordered list of typed blocks. Grow the trailing block as deltas arrive, once per frame, through a sanitizing Markdown renderer that tolerates unfinished input. Render tool calls as lifecycle cards, citations as numbered links, and artifacts as cards that open elsewhere. Keep partial content on Stop and on errors. Announce only lifecycle changes, through one polite status region.
do: Model the reply as an ordered list of typed blocks with stable ids, and key blocks by id, never by index
Grow only the trailing block, update the DOM at most once per animation frame, and never re-render or re-parse finished blocks
Use a Markdown renderer that tolerates unclosed fences, partial links, and partial emphasis, and sanitize every render
Allow links only for absolute http, https, and mailto URLs, and load images only from hosts the product allows
Render tool calls as cards with a readable name, a status line, and disclosures for the input and the result
Make each citation marker a link whose name starts with its visible number, with a preview that meets WCAG 1.4.13
Keep partial content on Stop and on errors, and offer Retry or Regenerate in place
Announce when a reply starts, runs a tool, ends, or fails, through one polite status region
Show reasoning only when the provider exposes it and the product chooses to, as a short status by default
Give every control a name, keyboard access, and a target of at least 24 by 24 px
dont: Store the reply as one growing string and re-parse it on every delta
Animate tokens one by one, or put the streamed text in a live region
Render model output as HTML without sanitizing it, or run code from it outside a sandbox
Pull the view down while the reader is scrolled up
Show the host's waiting indicator and this pattern's streaming cursor at the same time
Replace a reply that failed with a generic error
examples: A block list while streaming: [{ id: 'b1', type: 'text', state: 'final', content: 'Here is what I found.' }, { id: 'b2', type: 'tool-call', state: 'running', meta: { name: 'search_web' } }, { id: 'b3', type: 'text', state: 'streaming', content: 'The top results show' }]
The reader presses Stop halfway through: the text so far stays, the cursor goes, the reply is cancelled, and the status region says "Response stopped".
The connection drops mid-sentence: the partial sentence stays, an error block under it says "Connection lost", and Retry continues or regenerates the reply.
A reply contains an image from a host the product doesn't allow, with conversation data in its query string: the image doesn't load, and a link with its alt text shows instead.
A tool call that would send an email is held for approval: its card says it's waiting for approval, the cursor stops, and the reply is awaiting-review until the action is approved or rejected.

requirements.1.3.1: Blocks keep their structure (headings, lists, tables, and code), and a tool-call card exposes its name and state in text.
requirements.1.4.3: Text, code, citation markers, and tool-call labels have at least 4.5:1 contrast.
requirements.1.4.11: Icons, focus indicators, and the edges of controls have at least 3:1 contrast.
requirements.1.4.13: A citation preview that shows on hover or focus can be dismissed with Escape, stays while the pointer moves onto it, and stays until the pointer or focus leaves.
requirements.2.1.1: Every control, disclosure, and citation link works from the keyboard.
requirements.2.2.2: The cursor is steady, or stops blinking within 5 seconds.
requirements.2.4.7: Every control shows a visible focus indicator.
requirements.2.5.3: A citation link's name starts with its visible number, such as "1: Example Article, example.com".
requirements.2.5.8: Per-message controls are at least 24 by 24 CSS px.
requirements.4.1.2: Every control has a name, and disclosures say whether they are expanded.
requirements.4.1.3: Lifecycle changes are announced through one polite status region, without moving focus.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Moves through the message's links, controls, and disclosures in reading order.
keyboardNavigation.enterOrSpace: Activates the focused control or disclosure.
keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes a citation preview without moving focus.

screenReader.statusRegion: One element with role="status" per conversation, present before anything changes. In a chat the host renders it and this pattern announces through it; used on its own, this pattern renders it. While a modal dialog is open over the conversation, the region is inert, and anything to announce goes through a region inside the dialog.
screenReader.announcements: "Acme Assistant is responding" when the reply starts, the tool step while one runs ("Searching the web"), and "Response complete", "Response stopped", or the failure at the end. One short sentence at a time.
screenReader.neverAnnounced: The streamed text. A setting can optionally read each finished reply aloud.
screenReader.findingTheReply: A visually hidden heading at the start of the message (the host's, in a chat) lets people find the reply after "Response complete".

focusManagement.whileStreaming: Streaming and lifecycle changes never move focus.
focusManagement.stop: Stop keeps focus where it was: on the host's button, or on this pattern's Stop, which turns into Regenerate in place.
focusManagement.artifacts: Opening an artifact moves focus into its panel; closing the panel returns focus to the card.

blockModel.description: One reply is an ordered list of blocks: { id, type, state, content, meta }. Render every type; an unknown type renders as a labelled block of plain text, never dropped.

blockTypes.purpose: Prose, through the Markdown renderer. It may hold citation markers, and its links are underlined.
A fenced code block with its language. It renders before its closing fence arrives, has a Copy code button, and gets syntax highlighting once final.
A tool the assistant calls, with its result; see toolCallCard.
A source the text refers to; see citations.
Something shown elsewhere, such as a document, a file, or a chart; see artifacts.
A failure shown in place; see errors.
Only when the provider exposes a reasoning channel and the product chooses to show it; see reasoning.

messageLifecycle.description: The reply's states. The controls depend on them, and the AI Agent Chat Layout uses the same ones.

states.purpose: The request is accepted, and the reply's first content hasn't arrived; the host shows its waiting indicator
Blocks are added, or the trailing block grows
A tool call with consequences is held until someone approves it (with the AI Action Review Pattern); the reply waits for the person, not for the model
Stopped by the person; what arrived stays
Failed; what arrived stays, with an error block

transitions: idle to queued when the message is sent
queued to streaming on the first content
streaming to tool-running when a tool call starts running
streaming or tool-running to awaiting-review when a tool call with consequences is held for approval
awaiting-review to tool-running when it is approved and starts running
awaiting-review to streaming when it is rejected (its card becomes cancelled) and text continues
tool-running to streaming when text continues
any state before the end to complete when the reply finishes, to cancelled on Stop, or to errored on a failure it cannot recover from

streaming.trailingBlock: Text deltas grow the trailing text block and code deltas the trailing code block; another type starts a new block. Tool-call updates change their card by id, never by recreating it.
streaming.frames: Collect deltas and update the DOM at most once per animation frame (frameworkPatterns.frameBatching), and flush before the reply becomes complete, cancelled, or errored.
streaming.markdown: Re-render only the trailing block, from its full text, with a renderer that tolerates unclosed fences, partial links, and partial emphasis. Finished blocks never re-render. For long replies, re-parse only the last paragraph of the trailing block.
streaming.cursor: A CSS-only caret at the end of the growing block while the reply is streaming or running a tool; hidden while it awaits review and once it ends. It's steady, or blinks for 5 seconds at most.
streaming.motion: Don't animate tokens; whole blocks may fade in.

security.description: Model output is untrusted: prompt injection can put anything in it.
rules: Render Markdown through a sanitizer: no raw HTML from the model, or only an allowlist of harmless elements and attributes.

Links work only for absolute http, https, and mailto URLs; anything else, including relative links, renders as text (frameworkPatterns.safeUrls). Links to other sites get rel="noopener noreferrer", and a link that opens a new tab says so.

Images load only from hosts the product allows. Any other image URL could carry conversation data in its query string to another site without a click, so render it as a link with its alt text. The same goes for link previews the product fetches on its own. A Content-Security-Policy img-src is a second line of defense.
Tool inputs and results, file names, and citation titles render as text.

An artifact rendered as HTML or SVG goes in an iframe with the sandbox attribute, without allow-same-origin, and with allow-scripts only if it has to run code; ideally from a separate origin. The sandbox doesn't stop it from loading images, styles, or fonts from any host, which would send data out the same way, so give its document a Content-Security-Policy that allows requests only to hosts the product allows (artifactPolicy): as a header when it's served from its own origin, or as the first element of a srcdoc document. A srcdoc iframe also inherits the page's own policy. An artifact that runs code also needs script-src for that code, such as 'unsafe-inline' in a srcdoc document.

An artifact can also navigate its own frame to any URL, with data in the URL: through a link the person clicks, or, with allow-scripts, by its code or a meta refresh. Its own policy can't stop that, so the page that embeds artifacts limits frame-src to the origins it embeds on purpose (pagePolicy), or to 'none' when every artifact is a srcdoc document; a srcdoc artifact still loads and runs under it.

toolCallCard.description: A card per tool call, changed in place by its id.
surface: A readable tool name, not the internal id
A status line, in text, for the current state
A disclosure for the input, as labelled fields or JSON
A disclosure for the result or the error

states.indicator: The name and a muted placeholder
Status text with a subtle indicator, static under reduced motion
A one-line summary, such as a count or a title, with the full result behind the disclosure
What failed, with details behind the disclosure, and Retry when it is safe; the rest of the reply continues

citations: The marker is a link to the source (<a href>), since it navigates. Its name starts with its visible number, such as "1: Example Article, example.com".

A preview with the title, the domain, and a short snippet shows on hover and focus. It meets WCAG 1.4.13: Escape closes it, the pointer can move onto it, and it stays until the pointer or focus leaves. The popover attribute keeps it in the top layer, so overflow can't clip it.
A reply with three or more sources ends with a list of them.
A marker without a source is left out, never shown as a bare number.
implementationDetails.artifacts: Something too big for the message, such as a document, a file, or a chart, shows as a card with its title, type, and an Open button. Opening it shows the artifact in a side panel, a drawer, or full screen, moves focus there, and returns focus to the card on close. The card works as soon as it appears.
reasoning: Only when the provider exposes a reasoning channel and the product chooses to show it; otherwise there is no reasoning block, not even an empty one.
By default a short status, such as "Thought for 4s".
The full text only when the provider's terms allow it and the product needs it: a disclosure, collapsed by default. The answer stays visually first.

errors.description: Errors show in place, under what arrived, which stays.

kinds.recovery: Retry from where it stopped if the API supports it, otherwise Regenerate
Retry, with an optional countdown that is announced once, not every second
Show it as the reply's content; never cut it silently
In the tool-call card's error state; the reply continues

kinds.messaging: The reply was cut off at its length limit
kinds.recovery: Continue, if the API supports it

controls.perMessage: At the foot of a finished reply: Copy (the Markdown source), Regenerate, and Good and Bad response buttons (aria-pressed) with an optional comment; Retry sits on an error block. They show on focus as well as on hover, and always on touch screens. Icon buttons have names, such as "Copy response", and are at least 24 by 24 px. On phones, more than three go in a More actions menu.
controls.stop: In a chat, Stop is the host's: its send button turns into Stop and calls this pattern's stop, which keeps what arrived. Without a host Stop, show Stop at the foot of the streaming reply, available at once, turning into Regenerate in place.
controls.edit: Edit belongs to the person's message, which the host renders.
controls.share: Product-dependent. Before creating a link, say what it includes and who can open it.

implementationDetails.scrolling: The host's scroll area follows new content only while the reader is at the bottom; once they scroll up it stays put and offers a jump to the latest content. In the AI Agent Chat Layout the layout does this; elsewhere, the host does.
implementationDetails.responsive: On narrow screens, cards stack their parts, citation previews stay inside the viewport, and code blocks scroll sideways instead of wrapping.
performance: Coalesce deltas within one animation frame
Re-render only the trailing block, and keep finished blocks from re-rendering (memoize them by id)
Highlight code once its block is final
Load citation previews on hover or focus
Virtualize long conversations at the host, not inside one message

compositionWithChatLayout.description: With the AI Agent Chat Layout, the two divide the work instead of repeating it.
ownedByChatLayout: The shell, the transcript, and following new content
The waiting indicator before the first content
The Send and Stop button, and Edit on the person's messages
ownedByThisPattern: The blocks inside each assistant message
Tool-call cards, citations, artifact cards, reasoning, and error blocks
What to announce, through the layout's status region
coordinationRules: Hide the layout's waiting indicator as soon as this pattern's streaming cursor appears
The layout's Stop calls this pattern's stop, which keeps what arrived

compositionWithActionReview.description: With the AI Action Review Pattern, for tool calls with consequences, such as sending messages, changing records, payments, or sharing files. This pattern owns the tool-call card; the review pattern owns the approval surface, the confirmation rules, undo, and the audit trail.
handOffRules: A tool call with consequences stays pending until reviewed, and the reply moves to awaiting-review: the card's status line says it's waiting for approval, and the cursor and the running animation stop
Approval moves the action to approved; the card turns running only when the action starts running, cancelled on rejection, and error when running it fails, while the rest of the reply continues
Undo, retry, partial failures, and the audit trail belong to the review pattern; the card only reflects the result

The review's announcements go through the same status region, never a second announcer, except while the review is a modal dialog: the page behind it is inert, so the review announces through its own region inside the dialog
Only tool calls the product classifies as without consequences skip review: already authorized, read-only, sending no sensitive data out of the product, and costing nothing meaningful

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

safeUrls.description: The link and image checks for model output (implementationDetails.security). Use them in the Markdown renderer's or the sanitizer's rules for links and images.

frameBatching.description: Deltas collected and written at most once per animation frame (implementationDetails.streaming).

cursor.blink: Steady, or blinking for 5 seconds at most (WCAG 2.2.2)

toolStateChange.notes: A background or border change between states

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing blinks or fades, the running indicator is static, and scrolling never animates.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

must: Build on the project's message renderer, Markdown renderer, and sanitizer when it has them, and keep their APIs
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
Implement only the block types and controls the task needs
Sanitize every render, apply the link and image rules to model output, give HTML artifacts a sandbox and a Content-Security-Policy, and limit the page's frame-src
Keep partial content on Stop and on errors
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a Markdown parser, a sanitizer, or a syntax highlighter, without asking
Put the streamed text in a live region
Load images from model output from hosts the product doesn't allow
Show a reasoning surface when the provider doesn't expose reasoning
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: A streaming reply shows a cursor at its end that goes away when the reply completes, stops, or fails, and never blinks for longer than 5 seconds
Markdown with an unclosed code fence renders as a code block while it streams
Many deltas within one frame cause one DOM update, and finished blocks don't re-render
A tool call's card moves through pending, running, and success or error in place, with its state in text
A tool call held for approval puts the reply in awaiting-review: no cursor, no running animation, and Stop still works
Stop keeps what arrived, and a dropped connection shows an error under the partial content with Retry
Rate limits, refusals, timeouts, and truncation each show their own message
In model output, scripts never run, javascript: and relative links render as text, and nothing loads from, or navigates to, a host the product doesn't allow, including from inside an HTML artifact
A citation marker is a link whose name starts with its number; its preview opens on hover and focus and closes with Escape, and three or more sources get a list
A screen reader hears when a reply starts, runs a tool, ends, or fails, and never hears the streamed text
Copy, Regenerate, feedback, and every disclosure have names, work from the keyboard, and are at least 24 by 24 px
No reasoning surface shows when the provider doesn't expose reasoning; when one shows, it's a short status, collapsed by default
With reduced motion, nothing blinks, fades, or scrolls smoothly
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, and text and controls meet the contrast minimums in light and dark themes

relatedPotions.description: Optional: the chat shell this pattern fits into. The layout owns the transcript, the Send and Stop button, Edit, scrolling, and the conversation's status region; this pattern owns the inside of each assistant message, and the layout's waiting indicator hides when its streaming cursor appears.

Optional: the approval surface for tool calls with consequences. The card stays pending while the action is reviewed, turns running only when it starts running, cancelled on rejection, and error when it fails. This pattern owns the card; the review pattern owns approval, undo, and the audit trail.
Optional: feedback outside the message, such as a failed Copy.
Optional: confirmations, such as deleting an artifact, and the full-screen view of an artifact.
Optional: tool-call cards, citation previews, and code blocks use the theme tokens, so they stay readable in both themes.
